attack_narrative: The host exhibits a high baseline of internal process injection and anonymous memory threads, which appears to be standard security agent behavior on this system. During the incident, a highly anomalous and previously unseen executable named f6827dc5af661fbb4bf64bc625c78283ef836c6985bb2bfb836bd0c8d5397332.exe (PID 4544) was executed. This process utilized a Base64-encoded command line, generated network traffic, and triggered DLL name spoofing alerts. Concurrently, a new instance of DismHost.exe (PID 6520) was initiated out of a temporary AppData directory. Widespread system processes, including explorer.exe (PID 1528) and the Velociraptor monitoring agent (PID 2328), simultaneously experienced massive spikes in their anonymous memory thread and DLL counts. No threat intelligence sources flagged the observed file hashes or connection IPs, suggesting a localized or highly customized anomaly rather than a known threat campaign.
what_happened: A new, unnamed hexadecimal binary (PID 4544) executed with an obfuscated Base64 command line and performed network activity. A secondary new process, DismHost.exe (PID 6520), ran from a temporary AppData directory. Widespread anonymous memory thread and DLL count spikes were recorded across multiple pre-existing system processes. Comparison against the baseline confirmed that anonymous memory threads are highly prevalent on this host, though they escalated severely in count during this incident.
why: While the extensive process injection alerts are heavily mitigated by their presence in the host baseline, the introduction of a completely new executable (PID 4544) with Base64 obfuscation and network activity represents a critical, unexplained deviation. Running DismHost.exe (PID 6520) out of AppData further points to potential defense evasion. Because these highly suspicious features are entirely absent from the baseline, they elevate the host status to Suspicious despite the threat intelligence returning no known malicious matches.

key_evidence.signal: Base64 Command Line and DLL Name Spoofing
key_evidence.significance: This is a brand-new process exhibiting heavy command-line obfuscation and library anomalies that strongly suggest defense evasion.
Running system binaries from temporary user directories is highly anomalous and commonly associated with execution hijacking.
An escalation from 1001 to 5539 anonymous threads indicates massive scaling of memory instrumentation during the incident.

severity_assessment.rationale: The verdict aligns with the fused host score of 40.0 (Suspicious) because the widespread process injection is clearly baseline-consistent agent activity, but the new obfuscated binary (PID 4544) requires manual verification.

alternative_explanations: The massive thread and DLL spikes across existing processes are likely benign overhead from the local Velociraptor and monitoring tools, as they existed at baseline. The new hex-named process (PID 4544) and DismHost.exe (PID 6520) could theoretically represent a customized administrative installation script, though the use of Base64 makes this less likely.
recommendations: Isolate the host from the network to prevent potential command-and-control communications from PID 4544.
Decode and analyze the Base64 command-line payload used to launch PID 4544.
Inspect the temporary directory associated with DismHost.exe (PID 6520) to check for sideloaded DLLs.
Verify with system administrators if any software deployments or DISM updates were scheduled at the time of the incident.

attribution.rationale: The clear presence of Base64 obfuscation (T1027) and a system binary executing from an unconventional user path (T1036) point directly to execution and evasion techniques, though lack of threat intelligence prevents family attribution.
